business.title: A haplotype reference panel constructed from 490,319 UK Biobank genomes improves genotype imputation for global populations
business.desc: Here we constructed a genotype imputation reference panel from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank (UKB) participants1 and enabled both standalone and cloud-based phasing and imputation through EagleImp2 and EagleImp-RAP within the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform. The UKB reference panel achieves lower phasing switch error rates than the widely used TOPMed r3 panel (133,597 individuals) for all global superpopulations except AMR and for 25 of 26 1000 Genomes Project subpopulations. Imputation accuracy, measured by MAE, improved for 4 of 5 superpopulations and 12 subpopulations for variants with minor allele frequencies down to 0.01%. Estimated squared correlation further improved across all 5 superpopulations and 22 subpopulations, with the largest gains in East and South Asian populations. Reimputation of COVID-19 genome-wide association study datasets from Italy, Germany, Spain and Norway3,4 demonstrated that common-variant imputation remains unsaturated, enhancing the discovery of genome-wide significant loci and improving fine-mapping resolution. A haplotype reference panel constructed from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank participants improves genotype imputation accuracy across diverse populations and achieves lower phasing switch error rates than existing approaches.

business.title: Gold falls toward $4,000 as core PCE rises, U.S. growth accelerates - Kitco AM Report
business.desc: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Thursday, as stronger-than-expected U.S. economic growth and another increase in inflation reinforced expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening before year-end. The latest third-quarter gross domestic product and September personal consumption expenditures inflation reports highlighted the economy's resilience and persistent price pressures, limiting precious metals' ability to benefit from renewed diplomatic efforts involving the United States and Iran. Spot gold was trading near $4,026.20 an ounce, down $40.40, or 0.99%, while spot silver was trading near $52.590, down $1.256, or 2.33%.The U.S. economy expanded at a stronger-than-expected pace in the third quarter, while the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge accelerated in September. The advance estimate of gross domestic product showed the economy growing at an annualized 3.4% rate, above expectations for a 3.1% increase and accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter. Consumer spending increased 3.8%, while fixed investment surged 19.4%, reflecting continued strength in household demand and substantial business investment, particularly in artificial intelligence-related infrastructure. The expansion highlights the resilience of economic activity despite elevated borrowing costs and growing pressure on interest rate-sensitive industries.The September personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.5% on the month, its largest monthly gain in six months, while the annual inflation rate accelerated to 3.6% from 3.4% in August. Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, rose 0.3% on the month, matching expectations, while the annual core rate increased to 3.1% from 3.0%. The reports indicate that underlying inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's 2% target despite restrictive monetary policy. The combination of stronger economic growth, resilient consumer spending and elevated inflation strengthens the argument for maintaining higher interest rates and reinforces concerns that the Fed may need to resume tightening in December.Market positioning remains focused on the prospect of another Federal Reserve rate increase before year-end following Wednesday's decision to leave the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00%. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to maintain the current range, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favoring a 25-basis-point increase. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged continued economic strength and elevated inflation while leaving the possibility of additional tightening open. Interest rate futures indicated an approximately 83% probability of a 25-basis-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. Thursday's GDP and PCE figures reinforce those expectations, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield trading near the 5.0% area after rising to approximately 5.044% Wednesday. Higher nominal and real yields continue to increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, while the dollar's relative strength has added to selling pressure on precious metals.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remains a significant source of uncertainty in global energy markets, although fresh diplomatic efforts have reduced immediate concerns about another military escalation. U.S. Vice President JD Vance has sought to revive negotiations by sending a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei, with Washington seeking renewed discussions on Iran's nuclear program and broader security arrangements. Qatari mediators have also presented a new proposal aimed at ending the conflict, although a senior Iranian official dismissed the latest framework as unacceptable. Tehran continues to demand relief from the U.S. naval blockade, sanctions and restrictions on oil exports, while Washington insists that negotiations address Iran's nuclear activities. The differences leave the prospects for a near-term settlement uncertain, particularly as the possibility of renewed U.S. military action remains unresolved.Continuing attacks by Iranian-aligned Houthi forces against Saudi Arabian targets and threats to commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have complicated the diplomatic efforts. Saudi air defenses intercepted a missile aimed at the kingdom's Eastern Province, while earlier Houthi claims of an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery have not been accompanied by confirmation of a major operational disruption. Crude oil prices declined Thursday as hopes for renewed negotiations reduced some of the immediate geopolitical risk premium, with Brent crude retreating toward $114.00 a barrel and WTI falling near $101.00. However, the continuing threat to Gulf energy infrastructure and maritime traffic has prevented a more substantial retreat in oil prices, leaving the market exposed to further supply disruptions.For gold, the decline in crude oil prices offers some relief from energy-driven inflation expectations, but Thursday's strong GDP and persistent core inflation figures have reinforced expectations for restrictive U.S. monetary policy. The unresolved Gulf confrontation continues to support defensive demand, although higher real yields and the possibility of additional Fed tightening remain significant headwinds. Silver has suffered heavier selling pressure as concerns about restrictive monetary policy and industrial demand compound the broader precious metals weakness. The divergence between continuing geopolitical risk and falling bullion prices underscores the dominant influence of interest rate expectations and investment positioning.Global equity markets were weaker before the U.S. open as investors assessed the stronger U.S. economic data, persistent inflation and the implications for corporate borrowing costs. S&P 500 and Dow futures declined following the GDP and PCE releases, while Nasdaq futures remained volatile as investors digested quarterly results from major technology companies and continued concerns about artificial intelligence-related capital spending. European equity markets were mixed to weaker, with investors assessing regional economic data and Thursday's European Central Bank monetary policy decision. The ECB is scheduled to announce its decision at 9:15 a.m. EDT, followed by President Christine Lagarde's news conference at 9:45 a.m. EDT. The Bank of Japan also concludes its policy meeting Friday, adding another potential source of volatility in global currency and bond markets.The key outside markets see Nymex WTI crude oil prices lower and trading near $101.27 a barrel, while Brent crude was near $114.05. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is trading near the 5.0% area following Wednesday's increase. The U.S. dollar remains supported by expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening, while the retreat in crude oil prices is providing limited relief for precious metals following the stronger GDP and inflation readings. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)Technically, spot gold bulls' next upside price objective is to push prices back above the $4,084.00 to $4,146.00 resistance zone, with a sustained move through that area needed to reverse the near-term bearish technical trend. Bears' next near-term downside price objective is a break below $4,024.00, with a deeper downside target at $3,986.00. First resistance is seen at $4,084.00 and then at $4,146.00. First support is seen at $4,024.00 and then at $3,986.00.Spot silver bulls' next upside price objective is to drive prices back above the $54.680 to $56.420 resistance zone, with a sustained move through that area needed to improve the near-term technical outlook. The next downside price objective for the bears is a break below $52.690, with a deeper downside target at $51.300. First resistance is seen at $54.680 and then at $56.420. world.title: Putin Describes Russia and Africa as “Natural Allies” in Multipolar World Order
world.desc:
Addis Ababa, October 30, 2026 (ENA) — Russian President Vladimir Putin has described Russia and Africa as "natural allies" in shaping a multipolar, democratic world order anchored in international law, sovereignty, and equality.
Speaking on October 29 at the second plenary session of the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, the president emphasized the strong friendship and close partnership connecting the two sides.
“We are natural allies in building a multipolar, genuinely democratic world order, a world order free from diktat and double standards, based on respect for the norms of international law and the fundamental principles of the UN Charter in their entirety and interconnectedness,” he stated.
President Putin further reaffirmed Russia’s interest in supporting African countries as they defend their sovereignty, pursue independent development, and strengthen their economies and social sectors.
He also expressed Moscow’s readiness to maintain close cooperation with African nations to advance these shared objectives.
Highlighting the growing economic partnership, the President said Russian companies have been implementing major investment projects across Africa in various sectors, including energy production, peaceful nuclear energy, mining, industrial cooperation, logistics, and tourism.
Russian businesses, he noted, conduct their operations with integrity and respect for their African partners, emphasizing equality and mutual benefit in their engagements.
“They work on an equal footing with their partners and, rather than extracting profits as the former colonial powers once did,” he noted, adding, “they do the opposite: they invest and reinvest their earnings in the development of your national economies”.
He added that Russian companies also share advanced technologies and expertise, engage local subcontractors, establish production facilities and create employment opportunities.
Russia’s role as a reliable supplier of food and agricultural products to African markets has been supporting food security across the continent, Putin underscored.
Turning to peace and security, he said Russia, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, contributes to resolving existing conflicts and preventing new ones in Africa.
“In doing so, we consistently adhere to the fundamental principle you yourselves have proclaimed: African solutions to African problems,” he stressed.
The president also said Russia was undertaking various initiatives to support African countries in maintaining domestic stability, strengthening security and enhancing their defense and law enforcement capabilities.

world.desc: Moscow (SUNA) - President of the Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, arrived in the Russian capital, Moscow, at the head of the Republic of Sudan's delegation participating in the Third Russia-Africa Summit.
